question.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={log}_{2}⁡(u),\,u=2x+3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2}{(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
